unresolved.finding: Paths, username, and password are concatenated unquoted into a shell command, so spaces or metacharacters can change transfer arguments or execute unintended commands.
Transfer return codes are ignored and diagnostics discarded, allowing failed uploads to produce success messages and a download index containing unavailable binaries.
An unconditional yes is piped to pscp, accepting an unverified host-key prompt without establishing the intended server identity.
The password is carried in process arguments and the generated shell command line, exposing it to command-line inspection.
Discovery and path splitting assume bindir ends with a separator, so a normal directory argument without that suffix can shift platform and configuration fields or match sibling prefixes.
Every zip in a configuration directory is uploaded under the same revision-derived name without checking its provenance, so stale or multiple archives can overwrite the intended release.
An empty glob result still replaces the download page with an empty list and reports copying complete.
Argument parsing and distribution run unconditionally at module import, so importing the helper can raise an argument error or trigger publication.
The source path is interpolated into a TeamCity message without escaping service-message delimiters or line breaks.
The devnull stream opened for each transfer is never explicitly closed.
Executable paths, credentials, and transfer paths are interpolated unquoted into a shell command, so spaces or shell metacharacters can corrupt arguments or execute unintended commands.
The upload subprocess return code is ignored and both output streams are discarded, allowing failed binary transfers to be reported as finished and listed in the published index.
Piping an unconditional yes to pscp accepts an unverified host-key prompt instead of requiring a known server identity.
The password is supplied through process arguments and embedded in the shell command line, exposing it to command-line inspection.
connect stores the requested port but put never passes it to pscp, so nondefault SSH ports are ignored.
Every archive entry uses only fname, flattening nested directories and creating duplicate names or breaking relative-path dependencies.
Missing configuration directories are silently skipped and the download index is still replaced, so incomplete or entirely absent build outputs can publish an incomplete or empty release page.
Each upload opens a devnull stream without explicitly closing it, relying on interpreter cleanup rather than the client's no-op close method.
The binary destination is built by concatenating targetdir and 'bin/' without requiring or adding a trailing separator.

Contour extraction assumes contourf exposes patch children with scalar FaceVertexCData, so graphics implementations with different contour objects can leave the polygon arrays empty and make reindexing fail.
Polygons are matched only by contour level, so multiple disconnected polygons at the same level reuse one matching patch and can lose or duplicate geometry.
The ismember result is used directly as an index without checking for zero, so any contour level absent from the extracted patch data causes invalid indexing.
Removing all NaN separators before creating one patch joins separate polygon rings and can fill regions or holes that the original contour kept separate.
Combined plots copy exactly four patches by child order rather than threshold identity, making the selected boundary regions depend on contour count and graphics stacking order.
Three-panel PNG exports use a 3:1 size while their EPS counterparts use 2:1, yielding inconsistent aspect ratios and layout across output formats.
Line handles are assigned into arrays initialized as numeric empty arrays, which is incompatible with MATLAB graphics versions that return object handles.
The generated batch file unconditionally moves the redirected .new file over the original even if findent fails or is unavailable, potentially replacing source with empty or partial output.
Generated redirection and move operands are unquoted, so source filenames containing spaces or shell metacharacters are parsed incorrectly.
Input discovery and output location depend on the caller's current directory rather than the MATLAB function's location, allowing invocation elsewhere to generate an empty or misplaced batch file.
The script does not check fopen or fprintf results, so an unwritable destination or partial output is not handled explicitly.
Approximate comparisons only fail on a greater-than test, so NaNs and unequal infinities can pass without recording an assertion failure.
The relative-error threshold sums absolute magnitudes before scaling, allowing large finite inputs to overflow the threshold and pass despite substantial differences.
Every runtests call resets test numbering and reloads the previous suite's last_test, so the documented multiple-call workflow can skip tests in later suites and label completed work as crashed.
Started and completed tests persist the same true marker, while crash recovery only updates failed_asserts and neither increments nofails nor emits a failure hook.
The footer marks the previous test as crashed whenever no test ran, including a legitimate empty suite, and can duplicate the crash marker already emitted during restart.
Array size and shape mismatches increment nofails and invoke the hook but never update HTML failure state, so their test rows can be rendered as OK.
Array comparison routines always pass addtext=false, suppressing the assertion description on every HTML difference row.
Premature EOF or read errors report a file comparison failure without incrementing nofails, leaving the overall failed-assertion total incorrect.
File-comparison early returns leave whichever input files opened successfully connected instead of closing them.
Fixed-length line and token reads silently discard text beyond 200 characters per line or 20 characters per token, allowing differing files to compare equal.
List-directed tokenization errors are ignored and missing tokens use the real text sentinel '?', so malformed or slash-terminated records and literal question-mark tokens can hide differences.
File numbers are parsed into default REAL, so differences below single-precision resolution disappear even when the requested tolerance is tighter.
The runner terminates with bare STOP regardless of nofails, so process-exit-based CI can report success after failed assertions.
Test descriptions, compared strings, and file contents are emitted as raw HTML, allowing ordinary angle brackets and ampersands to alter or conceal report content.
Double-precision comparison failures are printed with only five to eight significant digits, which can display distinct failing values as identical.
Test names and failure text are inserted into TeamCity service messages without escaping quotes, pipes, brackets, or line breaks, allowing ordinary descriptions to break CI test reporting.
The three-dimensional real writer serializes dimensions as REAL while its reader interprets them as INTEGER, corrupting array extents and potentially causing enormous allocations.
Array readers validate type and rank but allocate directly from unchecked file extents, allowing negative dimensions to become empty arrays or excessive dimensions to terminate allocation.

Array retrieval unconditionally allocates a new pointer target without releasing an existing target or documenting that the incoming pointer must not own storage, permitting leaks on repeated retrieval.
Detected open and format failures use bare STOP, which normally exits successfully and can make a failed test-data load appear successful to a process-level test runner.
Payload reads and all writes omit IOSTAT handling, so truncated data or output failures abort in the runtime instead of producing a controlled storage error.
The fixed format version records default-kind binary values without recording their widths, endianness, or record-marker format, leaving cross-compiler and compiler-option compatibility unspecified.
Character retrieval error messages incorrectly identify the expected or retrieved data as complex.
All MPE status returns are ignored, so event-ID allocation or log-writing failures can remain invisible while the example reports successful numerical output.
The filename fallback checks argv but not argc or argv[0], allowing a null filename when the argument vector is present but empty.
The root's formatted input has no IOSTAT or end/error branch, so EOF or malformed input terminates that process while other ranks can remain waiting in MPI_BCAST.
An interval count near the default integer limit can overflow the DO iteration count or final induction-variable increment.
The example uses logging without MPE_Init_log or MPE_Finish_log and does not state that it requires an MPI profiling wrapper to initialize and flush logging.
MPE return codes are repeatedly overwritten without checks, so logging failures can leave undefined event IDs or missing output while numerical execution appears successful.
Negative interval counts pass the zero-only exit check and produce an empty integral reported as a pi approximation.
For interval counts near INT_MAX, the final i += numprocs can overflow signed int before the loop condition is rechecked.
The CLOG_IMPL interface uses FILE without including stdio.h, making compilation depend on an undocumented prior include.
APIs return pointers to communicator-ID records while the exposed set contains a growable table, but no lifetime or invalidation rule is stated for those returned pointers.
CLOG_MAXTIME is claimed to exceed all times but is a finite 100000000-second sentinel without a stated bound or time origin that guarantees the claim.
CLOG_int32_t is __int32 while i32fmt requests long, leaving a variadic type mismatch on compilers where __int32 aliases int even though Win32 gives both types equal width.
CLOG_UUID_SIZE expands to an unparenthesized sum, so expressions multiplying or dividing by this public size macro evaluate incorrectly.
Event APIs accept an un-sized const char pointer without stating whether callers must supply a full MPE_LOG_BYTES buffer or may pass shorter strings, leaving the required readable extent unclear.
MPE_Errors_to_dbx is declared outside the extern-C block, unlike the other C MPE routines, risking unresolved C++ linkage when used as an error handler.
MPIX and PMPIX generalized-request extension prototypes appear after extern-C closes, giving C++ callers mangled linkage for functions exposed by a C library.
The feature list defines MPIIMPL_HAVE_MPI_TYPE_CREATE_DARRAY twice and omits the corresponding subarray-constructor feature despite declaring that constructor.
Including mpio.h first from C++ can reach mpicxx.h through this circular include before mpio.h has defined MPIO_Request, while the C++ File methods require that type.
NULL_COPY_FN sets flag=true without initializing attr_out, advertising a successful attribute copy with an undefined output pointer.
Cartcomm::Sub always copies ten remain-dimension flags, reading past shorter valid inputs and supplying an undersized temporary for topologies with more than ten dimensions.
Alltoallw sizes and copies datatype arrays using local Get_size even on an Intercomm, although unequal remote-group sizes require different array lengths.
Alltoallw dereferences the send-datatype array before MPI can ignore it for an in-place operation, so an otherwise valid ignored null argument can fail in the wrapper.
Spawn_multiple copies array_of_info on every rank even though spawn inputs are only significant at the root, potentially dereferencing ignored arguments on nonroot ranks.
Temporary-output copy loops use supplied capacities rather than actual result counts or completion flags, reading uninitialized datatype, status, or topology entries on valid partial-result calls.
Raw temporary arrays are freed and modified request handles copied back only after error-handler calls, so a thrown MPI exception leaks allocations and can leave caller request handles stale.
Scalar-returning wrappers return uninitialized output locals if the invoked error handler returns after an MPI failure.
Clone ignores MPI_Comm_dup status and constructs a communicator from potentially uninitialized ncomm instead of applying the error-handling path used by Dup.
Grequest::Start is declared as an instance member, preventing the class-level factory invocation expected from a request-creation operation.
MPIR_ARGUNUSED is documented as removed at the end of the header but remains defined after the namespace closes.

MPIFCMB6 containing MPI_ERRCODES_IGNORE lacks the DLLIMPORT directive supplied for every other sentinel common block, risking a separate local sentinel address or unresolved import in Windows Fortran clients.

MPIO_Request aliases MPI_Request and its wait/test routines, but MPIO_REQUEST_NULL is hard-coded to zero instead of MPI_REQUEST_NULL, requiring a null-handle equivalence the header does not establish.
The nonblocking-I/O comments claim generalized requests are unimplemented even though this configuration explicitly enables them and aliases the request operations.
The claim that attribute external and internal types are identical omits the eight-byte integer setters' conversion to nf90_int in the included attribute implementation.
Numeric getters pass buffers to legacy routines without checking attribute length, so an attribute longer than the supplied array or scalar temporary can overwrite memory.
Eight-byte integer setters narrow values to default integer before the library can report range errors, allowing out-of-range values to be silently corrupted.
The attribute-ID lookup status is unconditionally overwritten by the subsequent attribute inquiry, obscuring any distinct failure of the requested attnum lookup.
Inquiry and getter wrappers copy uninitialized local outputs after failed calls, and integer array getters also copy undefined tail elements when the destination exceeds the attribute length.
